question: A boy of mass $50$ kg is standing on a weighing machine placed on the floor of a lift. The machine reads his weight in newtons. The reading of the machine if the lift is moving upwards with a uniform speed of $10\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ is ($g = 9.8\ \text{m/s}^2$)
solution:
At uniform velocity the acceleration is zero, so the normal force equals the weight:
$$N = mg = 50 \times 9.8 = 490\ \text{N}$$

The speed of the lift does not matter; only its acceleration does.
